reason: The hypothesis relies heavily on E1, which demonstrates a 57% residual stress reduction via preheating in mold steel. However, E1 does not address AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy alloys, and the claimed transferability of the mechanism and quantitative stress reduction to a completely different material system is unsupported by the cited evidence. The link between reduced stress and improved mechanical properties is also not directly evidenced in E1.
premises: Substrate preheating to ~300 °C reduces thermal gradients in AM
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual stress accumulation
Residual stress reduction of ~50–57% is achievable via preheating
Reduced residual stress leads to more uniform microstructure and improved mechanical properties
The cited evidence (E1) on mold steel is directly transferable to AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy alloy
